note_revisions.from_note: A najis vessel dipped in running water as seven jiryas pass: one washing or seven? Two wujūh; the ẓāhir of the aṣḥāb is one washing, and al-Qāḍī's Sharḥ says Aḥmad's words point to it. Here the madhhab side is the whole.
note_revisions.reason: English note names the Arabic term (problem register PR-02: «wash» is ghasl here); class, facts and expected unchanged

note_revisions.from_note: A thing received under a defective sale: the known madhhab position requires equivalent/value, not the named price, because compensation comes from loss under the hand, not this defective contract. Abu Bakr, followed here by Taqi al-Din, is reported as selecting the named consideration. Full paragraph read beyond the 400-character record cap.
note_revisions.reason: English note names the Arabic term (problem register PR-02: «void»/«defective» is fāsid here); class, facts and expected unchanged

note_revisions.from_note: Defective kitabah with a lawful named consideration: the source expressly says the named amount, not the slave's value, and reports agreement on that outcome. The full paragraph distinguishes a void undertaking with prohibited consideration, which is outside this encoding. The competing explanations (contract versus condition) are retained for human review; the guard tests the stated amount basis only.
note_revisions.reason: English note names the Arabic term (problem register PR-02: «void»/«defective» is fāsid here); then PR-03: «condition» is taʿlīq bi-ṣifa; class, facts and expected unchanged
